The mental game in coach-speak

Coaches often describe the mental side of shooting in short images: “trust it”, “let it go”, “stare it to death”. In English these images are easy to remember. Taken word for word, they can sound odd or even wrong in another language. Below are common phrases, grouped by moment, with what a coach usually means.

The rule for translating them is simple: pass on the meaning, not the picture. Choose one short equivalent for each phrase and keep it for the whole session or tour. Then the shooter can use it as his own cue word (Cue words and self-talk).

The plan

Before the call, coaches talk about the plan: “read the target”, “have a plan”, “commit to your break point”. The plan is a conscious decision, made while the targets are shown (in Compak® Sporting, often while watching the shooters before you). Once you call, many coaches want you simply to carry out that plan and make no new decisions, as part of your pre-shot routine (the same steps before each shot).

The eyes

Many phrases are about the eyes. “Soft eyes” means a relaxed, wide look (soft focus) at the pick-up point, the place where you expect to first see the target clearly. Then “hard focus” means a sharp look at one spot on the target, often its “front edge” (leading edge). “Don’t look at the barrel” means that your eyes stay on the target, while the gun stays at the edge of your vision.

Trust

“Trust it”, “let it happen” and “see it, shoot it” mean: stop checking and steering the gun, and let your trained movement do the work. Coaches also say “don’t check it” or “don’t measure it”. When your eyes go back to the barrels to check the gap, the hands often slow down with them, and the shot goes behind (stopping the gun). “Don’t ride it” is about time: it warns against riding the target, following it too long before the shot while it slows, drops or curls away.

Pairs

For pairs, “two separate shots” means that each target of the double has its own plan and its own break point. “Don’t chase the first one” means: after the first shot, take your eyes to the second target instead of watching the first one break (transition).

After a miss

After a miss you will hear “let it go”, “park it”, “reset” or “next target”. They all mean roughly the same: accept the miss, do your short reset and give the next target your full routine. Many coaches leave the analysis for after the round. More in Reset after a miss.

Score and attention

“One target at a time”, “process, not outcome” and “control the controllables” move attention away from the score, the weather and the squad, back to your own routine. More on process goals: Process goals and the score.

Tip: Many coach cues start with “don’t”: “don’t stop the gun”, “don’t look at the barrel”. Cues that say what to do instead, and what research says about them, are covered in Cue words and self-talk. If a coach uses many “don’t” cues, ask him before the session whether he wants them passed on as “do” cues, for example “keep the gun moving”. Do not change his words on your own.

Key points

  • Translate the meaning, not the image
  • Keep one fixed equivalent for each phrase for the whole session or tour
  • “Trust it”, “let it happen”: stop checking and steering the gun
  • “Let it go”, “reset”, “next target”: accept the miss and start fresh
  • If the coach invents a new image, ask what he means
Stand Talk

  • Coach One target at a time.

    Meaning: Forget the score and the last target: give this one target your full attention.

  • Coach Read the target.

    Meaning: Before you shoot, work out its line, speed and distance, and where it is easiest to break.

  • Coach Have a plan and commit to it.

    Meaning: Decide your points and the order while the targets are shown (in Compak® Sporting, often while watching the shooters before you), then shoot that plan without changing it mid-shot.

  • Coach Commit to your break point.

    Meaning: Shoot where you planned; do not let the shot drift further along the line.

  • Coach Soft eyes, then hard focus.

    Meaning: Look loosely at the pick-up area; once the target appears, lock your eyes sharply on it.

  • Coach Front edge.

    Meaning: Look at the leading edge of the target, not at the whole clay or at the gun.

  • Coach Stare it to death.

    Meaning: Keep an intense, unbroken focus on the target until the shot.

  • Coach Don’t look at the barrel.

    Meaning: Your eyes stay on the target; the gun stays at the edge of your vision.

  • Coach Trust it.

    Meaning: Stop checking the lead; let your trained movement do the work.

  • Coach Let it happen.

    Meaning: Do not force or steer the shot; let the swing and the shot come as you trained them.

  • Coach See it, shoot it.

    Meaning: When the picture is right, fire without second-guessing.

  • Coach Don’t ride it.

    Meaning: Do not follow the target too long trying to be sure; shoot when the picture is right.

  • Coach Keep the gun moving.

    Meaning: No pause at the trigger: the swing goes on through the shot.

  • Coach Two separate shots.

    Meaning: A pair is two targets, each with its own plan and its own break point.

  • Coach Don’t chase the first one.

    Meaning: After the first shot, move your eyes to the second target instead of watching the first one break.

  • Coach Let it go.

    Meaning: Accept the miss and stop thinking about it; the next target matters now.

  • Coach Reset.

    Meaning: Do your short routine after the shot and start the next target fresh.

  • Coach Process, not outcome.

    Meaning: Think about doing your routine well, not about the score.

  • Coach Control the controllables.

    Meaning: Spend your attention on what you can change, such as your routine and effort, not on the weather, the referee or the squad.

  • Coach Play your own game.

    Meaning: Shoot your own plan and pace; do not copy the shooter before you.

For the interpreter
  • Write your fixed equivalents on a small card before the session and use them each time. If the coach invents a new image, ask him briefly what he means, then translate the meaning.

Check yourself · 3 questions

  1. The coach says “Don’t ride it.” What does he mean?

    1. Put more weight on your front foot
    2. Do not follow the target too long
    3. Do not mount the gun too early
    4. Leave the second target alone
    Answer

    Do not follow the target too long

    “Riding” a target means tracking it too long to be sure. The target slows, drops or curls away, and the gun often stops.

  2. How should an interpreter translate “Stare it to death”?

    1. Word for word, keeping the image
    2. Leave it out: it is only a joke
    3. By its meaning: look hard at the target
    4. As a warning about the referee
    Answer

    By its meaning: look hard at the target

    Pass on the meaning, not the picture: the coach wants intense, unbroken focus on the target.

  3. After a miss the coach says “Let it go, next target.” What is the message?

    1. Accept the miss; focus on the next one
    2. Change the order of the targets
    3. Wait for the referee’s decision
    4. Let the next shooter go first
    Answer

    Accept the miss; focus on the next one

    Accept the miss, do a short reset and give the next target your full routine; many coaches leave the analysis for after the round.
